priority_score_formula: priority_score = recent_count * abs(pp_delta) -- rewards both real volume and real movement together. A 10pp swing on 5 reviews (score 50) ranks below a 3pp swing on 40 reviews (score 120), matching the product intuition that a moderate move backed by a lot of real signal deserves more attention than a dramatic move on a handful of reviews. Tunable: swap in recent_count**0.5 * abs(pp_delta) to dampen volume's influence, or multiply by baseline_total if categories with a thin baseline should also be discounted.
zone_a_min_volume_reasoning: 15 recent mentions -- well above the 5-mention floor used elsewhere just to judge whether a rate is measurable at all; this feed is answering 'what should someone act on this week,' which needs real confidence in the number, not just statistical measurability.

health_signal_reliability.watch_reason: Only ~1.1% of the sample by volume (2 of 180), but this is where an inaccurate or delayed signal has the highest real-world stakes of anything in this taxonomy — a missed cardiac irregularity detection is a different category of consequence than a wrong step count. Frequency rank should not determine how visible this category is downstream.

ai_coach.watch_reason: ~5.6% of sample volume for the parent overall, but ai_autonomy specifically — the sharpest complaint shape ("I can't turn this off") — is extremely thin: a full-dataset keyword check (see taxonomy_changelog.md, v2 Fix 1) found exactly one review in all 3,295 describing a user disabling the AI Coach and having it silently re-enable itself. It's kept as its own subcategory anyway, per the brief's instruction not to bury low-volume/ high-stakes signal, but "watch" here means "watch for more examples," not "confirmed at scale."
